newsitem.title: UK: Christies to auction "Dr Zhivago" love letters.
newsitem.headline: Christies to auction "Dr Zhivago" love letters.

text.p: Love letters written by Boris Pasternak to the woman who was his inspiration for Lara, the heroine of his book "Dr Zhivago", will be auctioned in London on November 27, auctioneers Christie's said on Monday.

The tragic love affair between Pasternak and his mistress Olga Ivinskaya inspired the Russian author to write his Nobel-prize-winning novel set during the Russian revolution and its violent aftermath.
"They are a monument of Russian culture," said Peter Collingridge, Christie's specialist in manuscripts and Russian works of art told reporters.
The love letters were "absolutely beautiful", he added.
Poems, manuscripts and the last love letter Pasternak wrote to Ivinskaya on his deathbed in 1960, are expected to fetch around 500,000 pounds ($800,000).

"Dr Zhivago" was made into a Hollywood blockbuster in 1965 starring Omar Sharif and Julie Christie. It won an Academy Award for best screenplay losing out to the "Sound of Music" in the best picture category.

The book was not published in Russia, but appeared in Italy in 1957. Although awarded the Nobel prize for literature, Soviet officials, who frowned upon the book's portrayal of the revolution, pressed Pasternak to refuse it.
The KGB, the former Soviet Union's secret police, took the poems and letters from Ivinskaya in 1960. She was imprisoned twice for her association with Pasternak.

Only a few of the documents were ever returned and the most precious papers are now to be sold by her heirs. Christie's said the documents are the "most important" Pasternak archive to come onto the market.
